originalTitle: OnlyFans for Therapy review – a brave and unsettling emotional exposure
summary: Veering from confident to crumbling, Verona Verbakel delivers a vivid show mixing humour with trauma
content: We are all familiar with the cliche of the influencer narrating their daily routines – or should I say, their journey? – and trying to convince us, and perhaps themselves, they are living their best life. We know, too, about the websites offering intimate access in exchange for cash. But what if the online medium were put to more honest purposes? What if, instead of endless positivity, it presented a painful recovery from trauma? It would, suggests writer and performer Verona Verbakel, be cheaper than paying for therapy. After a back-of-the-envelope calculation, she estimates she would need 2,599 sessions with a psychiatrist at £70 a time to get her through a lifetime of recovery. The cost, either in cash or in continued trauma, has to be paid by someone. The exposure in her solo show, OnlyFans for Therapy, is of the emotional not the naked body kind. It concerns a woman haunted by the abuse she suffered as a five-year-old and the additional anguish of an investigation when she was 18. Confident and assured one minute, she crumbles the next – the damage for ever just beneath the surface, raw and inescapable. Part of the Big in Belgium programme, Karolien De Bleser’s production has a characteristically Belgian disregard for theatrical convention. Verbakel’s role is to sit, stony-faced at a laptop, occasionally catching our eye, and seemingly indifferent to the content of the first-person videos she shows in sequence. At turns upbeat and tearful, Verbakel appears in videos that vary from lying in bed wearing a sleep mask and reciting a drily comic list of emotional triggers to the actor making painful expeditions to the scene of the original abuse and breaking down as she does so. The direct-to-camera honesty of the online world makes the pain all the more vivid in a brave, unsettling show. • At Zoo Playground, Edinburgh, until 30 August • All our Edinburgh festival reviews • In the UK, the NSPCC offers support to children on 0800 1111, and adults concerned about a child on 0808 800 5000. The National Association for People Abused in Childhood (Napac) offers support for adult survivors on 0808 801 0331. In the US, call or text the Childhelp abuse hotline on 800-422-4453. In Australia, children, young adults, parents and teachers can contact the Kids Helpline on 1800 55 1800; adult survivors can seek help at Blue Knot Foundation on 1300 657 380. Other sources of help can be found at Child Helpline International
chineseTitle: OnlyFans for Therapy评论——勇敢而令人不安的情感暴露
chineseSummary: 从自信到崩溃，维罗纳·维巴克尔呈现了一场将幽默与创伤融为一体的生动表演
chineseContent: 我们都熟悉有影响力的人讲述他们的日常生活的陈词滥调——或者我应该说，他们的旅程？ ——并试图让我们相信，也许还有他们自己，他们正在过着最好的生活。我们也知道一些网站提供亲密访问以换取现金。但如果在线媒体被用于更诚实的目的呢？如果它不是无尽的积极性，而是从创伤中痛苦地恢复怎么办？作家兼表演者维罗纳·韦尔巴克尔表示，这比支付治疗费用要便宜。经过粗略计算，她估计她需要接受 2,599 次精神科医生的治疗，每次费用为 70 英镑，才能让她度过一生的康复过程。代价，无论是现金还是持续的创伤，都必须由某人来支付。她的个展《OnlyFans for Therapy》中的展示是情感性的，而不是裸体的。故事讲述了一名妇女在 5 岁时遭受的虐待以及 18 岁时因调查而遭受的额外痛苦所困扰的女性。前一分钟还自信满满，下一分钟她就崩溃了——这种伤害永远隐藏在表面之下，原始且不可避免。卡罗琳·德·布莱瑟 (Karolien De Bleser) 的作品是比利时大制作计划的一部分，其作品具有比利时人特有的对戏剧惯例的漠视。维巴克尔的角色是坐在笔记本电脑前，面无表情，偶尔引起我们的注意，似乎对她按顺序播放的第一人称视频的内容漠不关心。维巴克尔出现在视频中，时而乐观，时而落泪，从戴着睡眠面罩躺在床上，背诵一系列冷幽默的情感触发点，到演员痛苦地探索最初的虐待现场，并在这样做时崩溃。网络世界直面镜头的诚实让痛苦在勇敢的场景中显得更加生动。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
